items.title: AbbVie’s Q3 beat should keep ‘train rolling’ as company eyes bolt-on deals
items.snippet: Strong immunology and neuroscience sales fueled AbbVie’s latest quarterly beat as the pharma’s stock continues to hit all-time highs.

items.title: Immutep, Molecular cut workforces
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: AstraZeneca employs $1.5B cost savings to reinvest back into growth
items.snippet: “You don't spend one and a half billion dollars without creating jobs,” AstraZeneca CEO Pascal Soriot said as the pharma announced a new cost savings program alongside third quarter earnings.

items.title: Regeneron achieves ‘clean sweep’ in Q3 with myriad pipeline catalysts on deck
items.snippet: Regeneron executives struck an upbeat tone on an investor call Friday as the biotech posted a consensus-beating $5.1 billion in third quarter earnings and CEO Leonard Schleifer touted the company’s ‘disease agnostic’ pipeline and approach to business development.

items.title: Sanofi targets late-phase and commercial M&A to offset looming Dupixent decline
items.snippet: Focused on ensuring growth beyond Dupixent, Sanofi wants to acquire derisked assets that may benefit from the French pharma’s commercial capabilities, executives said on Friday as they reported third-quarter earnings.

items.title: Acumen scraps sole asset after Alzheimer’s fail, plunging stock 80%
items.snippet: Acumen will implement cash-saving strategies and assess its options after sabirnetug failed to beat placebo, leaving the biotech without a clinical program.

items.title: ‘We need to do better,’ Alnylam CEO admits, as uncertainty looms over transthyretin franchise
items.snippet: Alnylam shares dropped by a quarter on Thursday, with analysts suggesting the decline puts the RNAi specialist within range for a takeout.

items.title: Once undruggable, the Wnt/B-catenin pathway shows increasing promise
items.snippet: Early-stage clinical data from our company and others point to the Wnt/β-catenin pathway as a new avenue for targeting multiple cancer types.

items.title: New biotech Setara forms with $90M to take on Jazz’s bonus rare disease programs
items.snippet: Setara Biosciences has formed around a handful of assets from Actio Biosciences, which was acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals earlier this year.

items.title: Dren Bio lands $350M to push rare blood cancer therapy toward market
items.snippet: After Sanofi paid $600 million in cash to acquire Dren Bio’s bispecific last year, the biotech has secured a hefty financing to fund late-stage development and commercial preparations for its lead asset.

items.title: Lilly’s guidance has jumped by $10B as GLP-1 sales keep blowing past expectations
items.snippet: With the commercial business performing so well, Eli Lilly is eyeing earlier business development bets to build out a longer-term pipeline.

items.title: Merck looks ahead to ‘another year of investment’ as Keytruda cliff looms
items.snippet: On its third-quarter earnings investor call Thursday morning, Merck executives touted recent pipeline wins alongside a strong performance for subcutaneous Keytruda and pulmonary arterial hypertension drug Winrevair that drove the pharma’s overall sales expectations to surpass expectations.

items.title: BMS drops Prothena-partnered neuro drug, sales outlook improves on a Q3 beat
items.snippet: In addition to canning an Orum-acquired blood cancer candidate last month, Bristol Myers Squibb cut a Prothena-partnered neuro asset in the third quarter. But with sales climbing 7%, the Big Pharma raised its full-year revenue forecast.

items.title: Ono cans 2 endocannabinoid drug studies after quintuple Phase 2 failure
items.snippet: Ono Pharma’s ONO-1110 failed five Phase 2 trials, leading to the discontinuation of development in depression and social anxiety. Work will continue for three pain indications.

items.title: Lilly can’t stop, won’t stop as revenue climbs 39% thanks to GLP-1 bestsellers
items.snippet: Eli Lilly’s shares rose 4% in early morning trading after reporting revenue of $24.4 billion, well past consensus estimates.

items.title: HHS clears compounding pharmacies to manufacture 6 unapproved peptides
items.snippet: Under the interim policy, officials do not intend to take action against sites that produce the peptides.

items.title: Stability, speed and strategy: Inside Australia’s early‑stage edge
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from Jerome Barley, commercial director at Avion Medical and Ryan Klein, vice president, business development, US and APAC at Resolian. We discuss why Australia has become a magnet for early clinical development, and whether its speed, regulatory clarity and tax incentives are...

items.title: Biopharma cuts at manufacturing plants expected to affect 4,000+
items.snippet: As companies invest billions of dollars to reshore manufacturing, 10 biotech and pharma businesses are reportedly trimming staff at manufacturing locations in 2026 or the coming years, with BioNTech having the deepest cuts.

items.title: 8 companies hiring in New York
items.snippet: Looking for a biopharma job in New York? Jobs on BioSpace have soared year over year and month over month.

items.title: Genmab’s cancer bispecific delivers early survival win in ‘exceedingly positive’ Phase 3 readout
items.snippet: Analysts hailed the Phase 3 head and neck cancer results as a big victory for an asset central to Genmab’s growth plans.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
